after-dark.title: Cotonou after dark
after-dark.intro: Follow the smoke, the music and the evening crowd on a food walk through the city’s most generous street kitchens.
after-dark.heading: Come hungry. Leave knowing the city better.
after-dark.p1: Street food is Cotonou in miniature: fast-moving, deeply social and full of exacting opinions.
after-dark.p2: With a local cook, start with hot talé-talé, cross town for grilled wagassi, and finish over peppered fish near the lagoon.

north-bound.title: North bound
north-bound.intro: Take the red road north: landscapes, living traditions and the pace of Atacora communities.
north-bound.heading: A slower way into the north.
north-bound.p1: The north is not a stopover. It is a set of places where food, craft and landscape still set the day’s rhythm.
north-bound.p2: Travel with time for guides, regional meals and the distances between villages.

on-the-water.title: On the water
on-the-water.intro: Two quiet hours with a local on the estuary—where river, fishing and Atlantic shoreline meet.
on-the-water.heading: Where river meets sea.
on-the-water.p1: Follow the estuary with someone who works it, not only visits it.
on-the-water.p2: Learn how tides, nets and meals structure the day along the Mono.

five-meals.title: Five meals · First days
five-meals.intro: Five dinners for your first five days in Benin—an invitation to eat like a local from day one, not as a tourist checklist.
five-meals.heading: Start living local at the table.
five-meals.p1: The first days in a country set the tone. Instead of defaulting to hotel menus, these five meals place you with hosts, street kitchens and family tables—so the country enters through taste, conversation and routine.
five-meals.p2: Each evening is a different entry: market heat, coastal fish, northern cheese, a home sauce, a shared celebration plate. Together they form a gentle curriculum for being present in Benin.

first-table.title: The First Table
first-table.intro: On the first day of the year, share a table at Place Chacha in Ouidah—including soupe joumou—on ground that holds both memory and living community.
first-table.heading: A first meal on historic ground.
first-table.p1: Place Chacha is where enslaved people were once sold. Today it remains a public square in Ouidah—a place of hard history and present life. The First Table invites visitors and locals to sit together on 1 January, with soupe joumou and other shared dishes, in a spirit of continuity rather than spectacle.
first-table.p2: This is not a reenactment. It is a contemporary gathering: food, presence, and the choice to begin the year at a table that does not forget where it stands. Context is offered with care; the meal is shared as equals.

market-to-kitchen.title: Market to kitchen
market-to-kitchen.intro: Shop the stalls with a local, then cook what you bought into a Beninese plate.
market-to-kitchen.heading: Buy it. Cook it. Sit down.
market-to-kitchen.p1: Choose ingredients at the market, follow them into a kitchen, eat what the day offers.
market-to-kitchen.p2: Not a show kitchen—a real market and a shared table.

ganvie-crossing.title: Ganvié crossing
ganvie-crossing.intro: A pirogue morning through the stilt city—with a guide who lives the water.
ganvie-crossing.heading: A city without streets.
ganvie-crossing.p1: Ganvié is home first. Early light, floating market hours, time to watch without turning life into a backdrop.
ganvie-crossing.p2: Come for the water; leave with how a town organizes itself on pirogues alone.

memory-walk.title: Memory walk · Ouidah
memory-walk.location: Place Chacha → Door of No Return
memory-walk.intro: Walk the historic path with context—without spectacle.
memory-walk.heading: History underfoot.
memory-walk.p1: Ouidah asks for slow steps and good guidance.
memory-walk.p2: Pair it with living Ouidah so the visit is not only about the past.

royal-ground.title: Royal ground · Abomey
royal-ground.intro: The Dahomey Kingdom landscape with a knowledgeable guide.
royal-ground.heading: Where the kingdom still speaks.
royal-ground.p1: Abomey is a living relationship to royal history and craft.
royal-ground.p2: Go with someone who can open context; leave room for silence.

aheme-day.title: A day on Lake Ahémé
aheme-day.intro: Cross and linger on Ahémé with a local boatman—thermal springs, lake villages and the slower Mono clock.
aheme-day.heading: Let the lake set the schedule.
aheme-day.p1: Ahémé is not a backdrop. It is work, transport and memory for the communities around it.
aheme-day.p2: Go with someone who knows the channels. Leave time for stillness, not only movement.

dantokpa-dawn.title: Dantokpa at dawn
dantokpa-dawn.intro: Enter West Africa’s great market before the heat peaks—with a guide who knows which aisles matter.
dantokpa-dawn.heading: The city starts here.
dantokpa-dawn.p1: Dantokpa is logistics, theatre and livelihood at once. Dawn is when you can still hear individual voices.
dantokpa-dawn.p2: Buy little. Watch more. Let your guide decide when to move and when to stop.

porto-morning.title: Porto-Novo before the heat
porto-morning.intro: A walking morning through markets, shaded streets and the capital’s layered architecture—before the city fully wakes.
porto-morning.heading: Meet the capital without hurry.
porto-morning.p1: Porto-Novo rewards early feet: Ouando’s first trades, quiet courtyards, and streets that still belong to residents.
porto-morning.p2: Finish with a local breakfast. The point is arrival into the day, not a checklist of monuments.

craft-hands.title: Hands that make
craft-hands.intro: Time in a workshop with makers—textiles, metal, appliqué or wood—where skill is demonstrated, not performed.
craft-hands.heading: Watch the work, not the souvenir shelf.
craft-hands.p1: Craft in Benin is knowledge held in hands and families. A good visit is slow and specific.
craft-hands.p2: Ask permission before photos. Buy only what you will use or truly keep.

savanna-morning.title: Savanna morning · Pendjari
savanna-morning.intro: An early drive into the reserve with a park guide—tracks, light and the chance of wildlife without guarantees.
savanna-morning.heading: Patience is the ticket.
savanna-morning.p1: Pendjari is not a zoo. Sightings depend on season, time and respect for the rules of the park.
savanna-morning.p2: Book through legitimate operators. The wild holds because people insist on limits.

lagoon-evening.title: Lagoon evening
lagoon-evening.intro: Late light on the lagoon—fishermen, smoke, and the soft border between city and water.
lagoon-evening.heading: Where the city exhales.
lagoon-evening.p1: Evening on Nokoué is less about a viewpoint than about watching work wind down.
lagoon-evening.p2: Stay long enough for the light to change. Leave before you become the noise.
